subject: Mid-Q OKR pulse: re-prioritization & dependency requests
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-Q OKR pulse: re-prioritization & dependency requests

Team —

This is the mid-quarter OKR checkpoint for Q2. I want a short, focused status so we can decide on any re-scopes before the QBR prep week. Please reply in-line with:

- Current RAG (green/yellow/red) for each OKR you own
- % complete (best estimate)
- Any proposed re-scope (concrete ask: which metric to relax, by how much)
- Blocking dependencies and ETA for unblock (owner + ticket/link)

I've attached an updated Q2_OKR-tracker.xlsx and a dependency-matrix.pdf — please update the tracker and add new rows to the matrix by EOD Monday (48 hrs). Key things I'm watching: throughput target for hosted API, latency p95 SLA, and SOC2 evidence for Dedicated.

Initial priorities to consider for re-scope:
- Defer non-critical throughput improvements in favor of latency fixes if we cannot get the extra GPU capacity by May 27
- If legal sign-off on data retention is delayed, we should limit Private deployment rollouts vs. expanding Dedicated capacity

Concrete asks for this thread:
1) Vivek — tell us whether dropping the end-to-end throughput target by 20% will materially change downstream revenue risk.
2) Monica — any customer renewals at risk this quarter if we change the SLA/throughput commitment (esp. Acme)?
3) Stephanie/Infra — confirm GPU node availability and CloudOps ETA (ticket INF-2312).

We need a decision from leadership by next Wednesday so QBR slides can reflect final scopes. Marking Markus to weigh in once we have the short updates.

Thanks — keep the replies short.

— Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q2_OKR-tracker.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), dependency-matrix.pdf (PDF stub)
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-Q OKR pulse: re-prioritization & dependency requests

Lauren — thanks for the clear ask. Status inline below.

OKR: Improve hosted API p95 latency from 220ms -> 160ms by end of Q2
- RAG: Yellow
- % complete: 45%
- Proposed re-scope: If we cannot secure +2 GPU nodes (A100 equivalent) for the inference pool by 2025-05-27, propose moving the p95 target to 175ms and keep the 160ms target as a stretch goal. This maintains customer-facing commitments but reduces risk of over-promising.
- Blockers & ETAs: CloudOps capacity request pending — ticket INF-2312 (CloudOps assigned, awaiting capacity approval). ETA from vendor (CloudOps Support) is May 26 if expedited; otherwise June 8. Also need SOC2 evidence for Dedicated config which is with Security (Sarah Li from Acme requested additional logs).

Notes: Dropping throughput target by 20% (as you suggested) would free up ~18% GPU time but latency improvements are more dependent on kernel-level optimizations and smarter batching — those are in flight (PRs linked on INF-2401) and won't be fully effective until new kernels land in staging next week.

Dependency asks (short):
- CloudOps Support: confirm expedited GPU allocation (INF-2312) by May 26.
- Security: provide SOC2 logs and evidence scope for Dedicated by May 22 so we can validate before the QBR.

I updated the tracker (Q2_OKR-tracker.xlsx) with the current percentages and added proposed re-scope text in the comments column.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Quick note from the revenue side — short answers:

OKR: Expand DedicatedARR by 15% this quarter (renewals & expansion)
- RAG: Yellow
- % complete: 38%
- Proposed re-scope: If throughput commitments on Hosted change materially we should offer Acme a short-term SLA addendum instead of changing the contractual commitment in their renewal. This keeps renewals on track while we fix infra.
- Blockers & ETAs: Procurement at Acme is waiting on documented Dedicated network topology and data retention SLA. Sarah Li (Acme) asked for the SOC2 log scope as well — they're pausing the final sign-off until they receive it. ETA if we provide the docs by May 22: they can sign the amendment by May 30.

Action items I've taken:
- Sent Acme a one-page SLA addendum draft (attached in my internal folder) and scheduled a follow-up with Sarah for Thurs 5/22.
- Added a note in the tracker under "customer risk" for Acme and linked the HubSpot record HS-98432.

If leadership decides to lower the throughput target, please confirm whether we should proactively offer the SLA addendum or wait for Acme to request changes. My recommendation: offer it proactively with an option to revert once we hit the original numbers.

— Monica Patel
Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Team — thanks for the updates and the updated tracker: I reviewed Vivek and Monica's notes. Quick leadership decision so we can lock slides for QBR prep: 

1) Approve proposed re-scope for latency: move p95 goal to 175ms as the committed target; keep 160ms as a stretch. This is contingent on CloudOps making best-effort GPU allocation by May 26. If they miss that date, we will communicate the change externally with the SLA addendum suggested by Monica.

2) Throughput target: do not lower the published throughput number yet. Instead, prioritize latency work and the canary rollout (see 3). If latency work frees up capacity, we will revisit throughput as an acceleration spot.

3) Canary plan: Vivek + Stephanie to run a 2-week canary starting May 28 scoped to 5% of Dedicated traffic. Report metrics after one week and at end of canary (INF-2503). If the canary is green, we will gradually roll to 25% by June 11.

4) Dependencies: Security (Stef) — provide SOC2 evidence scope & logs to Acme by May 22. CloudOps Support — expedite INF-2312; leadership expects an ETA by EOD May 23. Monica — continue with the proactive SLA addendum offer to Acme; coordinate messaging with Lauren and Legal.

I'll sign off on the QBR slides with this approach. Lauren, prepare a one-pager for the executive QBR slide that states the re-scope and the canary plan (bullet points).

— Markus Klein
CTO (interim)
Redwood Inference
